mcp_server.def: A small program that lets an AI assistant use an outside tool or data source through the Model Context Protocol, an open standard.

model.def: The trained AI system that produces text, images or other output. Products and agents are built on top of models.

agent.def: Software that uses a model to carry out multi-step tasks on its own, often by calling tools.

prompt.def: The instructions or text you give an AI model. A prompt template is a reusable one.

skill.def: A packaged set of instructions and files that teaches an AI assistant to do a specific task.

library.def: Reusable code that developers add to their own software.

dataset.def: A collection of data used to train or test AI models.

product.def: A finished AI app or service that you use directly, without writing code.

article.def: Writing about AI: a guide, tutorial or blog post.

paper.def: A research paper, usually from arXiv.

event.def: A conference, meetup, webinar or hackathon.

course.def: A course or a certification about AI. Its platform is listed under Platforms; tags say whether it gives a certification (a proctored exam) or a certificate of completion, and whether it is self-paced, instructor-led, a live event or an exam only.

other.def: An AI resource that fits none of the other types.

glossary.typeAssigned: The type comes from the source's data, keyword rules or an AI model, so it can be wrong.

license.def: The rules for using, changing and sharing the resource. Always read the license itself before relying on it.

open_source.def: The source code is public under a license that lets others use and modify it. It does not always mean free of charge.

tech_level.def: How much technical skill is needed to get started.

platform.def: Where it runs, for example web, desktop, mobile, command line, or a language runtime such as Python or Java.

popularity.def: Counts such as stars or downloads reported by one source. They are never combined into a single score.

provenance.def: Where a piece of information came from and when it was retrieved.

mission.title: Our mission
mission.lede: Help people find the right AI resource for their need, and show the proof behind every answer.

sections.title: Why helper2.ai exists
paragraphs: New AI models, tools, agents, MCP servers and papers appear every day. General search engines mix them with marketing pages and old content, so it is hard to know what is real and current.
We search only sources about AI, tell you which sources we searched, and show where every result comes from and when it was checked.

sections.title: What we promise
items: Proof before opinion. The guide only recommends a resource when it can quote a real source that supports the choice.
Honest coverage. We list every source we search and show what each one returned. We do not claim to search the whole web.
No invented facts. We never fill in dates, popularity or other facts that no source stated.
Open by default. The source code is public under the Apache-2.0 license.
Privacy first. In Europe, personalized ads and analytics only if you accept them, and we never sell data.

sections.title: How we mark AI text
items: On the screen, every text an AI model wrote or read has a mark next to it. A full dot ● is text a model wrote: the guide’s picks, reasons, search terms, question back to you, comparison and explanation, a name it did not find in our sources, a summary of a resource, and the English translation of a query. A half dot ◐ is a value a model read from a source, or a requirement it read from your question. A hollow dot ○ is a model’s estimate, which can be wrong. Point at a mark, or tap it, to read its words, such as “AI-written”, “Extracted by AI” or “AI-estimated”. The key is at the bottom of every page. The setup steps carry the note “Steps written by AI”. A setup step shows only the words of the tool’s own documentation, labeled “From the source”, when a second AI check could not confirm its text, or when the site is set to show every step only from the source.
On the home page, an example a model drafted and a person checked has a full-dot mark that reads “AI draft”, with the note “Drafted with AI, checked by a person”.
In the page, the same text carries the HTML attribute data-ai-generated="true", and data-ai-model with the model name when we know it.

In our API, a guide answer has an aiContent object that names the provider, the models and the fields they wrote. Catalog values carry an origin such as AI_SUMMARY or AI_EXTRACTED. A search gives the translation of a query in its own field, translatedQuery.
Quotes, titles and links are never written by AI. They come from the sources.

sections.title: Who is behind it
paragraphs: Silvio Incalza, a software engineer based in Switzerland, builds helper2.ai as an independent project. The AI guide runs on NVIDIA Nemotron models served by Nebius Token Factory.

how.title: How the guide answers
how.lede: Search first, an AI model second, a checker last. The model never decides what is true.

body.text: A fast Nemotron model turns your words, in any language, into search terms. A normal search across every source then finds up to {{maxCandidates}} real candidates.
body.withoutNumbers: A fast Nemotron model turns your words, in any language, into search terms. A normal search across every source then finds the real candidates.

body.text: A reasoning model picks at most {{maxPicks}} of those candidates and explains why with a quote.
body.withoutNumbers: A reasoning model picks a few of those candidates and explains why with a quote.

check.title: A validator checks
check.body: Each pick must be one of the candidates, and its quote must appear word for word in that resource’s text. Rejected suggestions are counted and shown.

notStated.title: Missing means not stated
notStated.body: If no source gave a fact, it says Not stated. Dates, popularity and prices are never filled in.

dates.title: Dates are the source’s own
dates.body: Published and updated come from the source. Otherwise you see when helper2.ai first saw it.

unchecked.title: Every explanation is labeled
unchecked.body: Code checks the quote word for word. A second model call checks the explanation; the page says if it was checked, removed or not checked.

fallback.title: Search keeps working
fallback.body: If the AI model is unavailable, the guide shows the top real results instead, clearly labeled.

support.title: Support helper2.ai
support.lede: You can use helper2.ai for free, with no account, and it stays that way. Running it costs money every day. If it saves you time, you can help pay for it.
costs: The AI models that write the guide's answers and read the pages about each resource.
Live web searches, paid per search.
The servers in Germany, the database and the backups.
The time to add sources, check results and fix what breaks.
